reason: The transporter-bearing cell and arriving glucose and oxygen suggest the first step in supplying fuel.
expectation: The cell will take in glucose for energy production.

effect: The cell first becomes a muscle fibre; glucose and oxygen must be used elsewhere in the energy sequence.
reaction: The automatic combination clarified the starting point, though I expected fuel uptake first.
reason: Mitochondria use glucose and oxygen to help supply energy, so these are a plausible pair.
expectation: This will begin the energy-production process needed to make ATP.

effect: Glucose and oxygen have fuelled the mitochondria, so ADP and phosphate are the likely next ingredients for making ATP.
reaction: The picture clarified that glucose is first split in the cell fluid before smaller molecules enter the mitochondrion.
reason: ADP and phosphate are the ingredients for ATP, which the muscle fibre needs for its work.
expectation: The fuelled mitochondria will produce ATP.

effect: The mitochondria produced an ATP supply, showing how the cell continually remakes ATP for its pulling machinery.
reaction: The returning ADP and phosphate make the cycle clearer.
reason: Thin actin and thick myosin filaments are the visible parts of the muscle's pulling machinery.
expectation: The filaments will form a contractile unit that can be fitted into the muscle fibre.

effect: The thin and thick filaments formed sliding filament units that appear ready to fit into the muscle fibre.
reaction: The overlapping filaments make the pulling arrangement easier to picture.
reason: The muscle fibre has spaces for contractile units, and the sliding filament units appear to fill them.
expectation: The sliding filament units will be fitted into the muscle fibre.

effect: The sliding filament units are now inside the muscle fibre, ready for the steps that let it pull and relax.
reaction: The fitting followed naturally from the fibre’s described spaces.
reason: A calcium signal reaches the filaments and is a plausible trigger for contraction.
expectation: The calcium signal will prepare or trigger the fibre’s filaments to pull.

effect: The fibre needed ATP before the calcium signal; its myosin heads are now reset while binding sites remain covered.
reaction: The compatibility feedback clarified the required order, which I had guessed incorrectly.
reason: The calcium signal is still available and should act on the ATP-ready fibre.
expectation: Calcium will expose binding sites and allow the fibre to pull.

effect: Calcium exposed the grip sites, allowing the filaments to slide and the fibre to shorten. The remaining goal is to make it relax.
reaction: The distinction between the fibre shortening and the filaments staying the same length is clear and useful.
reason: The calcium-pumping membranes should remove calcium from around the filaments so the fibre can relax.
expectation: Calcium will be pumped back into storage, allowing the muscle fibre to relax.

effect: The calcium pumps completed the cycle by returning calcium to storage, covering the grip sites and allowing the fibre to relax under an outside pull. The goal is complete.
reaction: It was interesting that relaxation also requires ATP.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the calcium signal was most worthwhile because the result explained how myosin pulls and showed that the filaments slide without shortening themselves.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial attempt to bring fuel into the cell was confusing: the cell instead combined automatically with the muscle fibre structures. The feedback clarified what to do, but the ordering was not obvious from the goal.

surprise.text: I expected the calcium signal to act on the filament-filled fibre immediately, but the game required the ATP supply first and showed myosin resetting.

arbitrary.text: The required order of adding ATP before calcium felt somewhat arbitrary until the result showed the myosin head resetting. The feedback gave it a clearer purpose.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested to see how this working fibre contributes to a larger body system; the ATP cycle and sliding-filament explanation made the construction meaningful.
